The test `testEqualsCS1` in the `StringUtilsTest` class is calling the `equals` method from `org.apache.commons.codec.binary.StringUtils` with arguments of type `StringBuilder`. However, the `equals` method in `StringUtils` actually takes arguments of type `CharSequence`. This discrepancy in argument types is causing the test to fail.

The `equals` method in `StringUtils` checks if the two `CharSequence` objects are equal by calling the `equals` method on the first object if both objects are of type `String`, and by performing a region match otherwise.

To fix this issue, the test `testEqualsCS1` should be updated to pass arguments of type `CharSequence` instead of `StringBuilder`.

Next, I will provide the suggested methods to be fixed.
```java
org.apache.commons.codec.binary.StringUtils.equals(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.CharSequence)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
